findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of a provider named literally "alias"
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" instead of the actual alias ("idp-alias-" + i / "idp-alias-20"). Consequently none of the 21 identity providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are removed after the test (the cleanup targets a non-existent provider and will either no-op or throw), leaking state into other tests in the class/realm and making counts in subsequent tests flaky. Same mistake appears at lines 303 and 425.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate semantics changed for all callers
findings.body: getLoginPredicate() now additionally requires that org-linked IDPs have `organization.broker.public=true`. This public static predicate is used by callers outside the new invalidation logic (e.g. identity provider beans/filters); any caller that previously accepted org-linked, non-public IDPs will now silently drop them. This behavioural change is not documented in the enum's javadoc and could change which brokers are shown/accepted in flows unrelated to the login page.

findings.title: getForLogin cache is not invalidated on organization changes
findings.body: Unlike getByOrganization(), which checks `isInvalid(orgId)`, getForLogin() only checks the login cache key. If an organization is disabled, removed, or its IDP links change outside IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() (e.g. OrganizationProvider operations that only invalidate the organization entry), the cached ID sets for ORG_ONLY/ALL remain stale. The PR compensates only in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean by re-checking isEnabled() on the wrapped model; other consumers of getForLogin() get IDPs of disabled/removed organizations. Consider also checking isInvalid(organizationId) and registering login invalidation on organization updates/removal.

findings.title: remove() now always performs a DB lookup by alias
findings.body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now executed unconditionally at the start of remove(), even when the alias is present in the cache (previously the DB lookup only happened on the invalidated path). This adds an extra query to every IDP removal. The cached CachedIdentityProvider could be reused to build the model needed for registerIDPLoginInvalidation.
